title: In the United States, CPSC prints the poison line as 800-222-1222
summary: CPSC says to lock medicines and cleaning products away, because child-resistant caps are often not childproof, and it prints the US poison line 800-222-1222.
body: CPSC says latches and locks on cabinets and drawers help keep children from medicines, laundry detergent, household cleaners, matches, and cigarette lighters, and from knives. Even products with child-resistant packaging should be locked and kept out of reach, because that packaging is often not childproof. If a caregiver suspects a child swallowed a poisonous substance, the page says to contact the poison control hotline at 800-222-1222. That number is the United States line as this page prints it. It is not the world's number. Europe's emergency number, on a European Commission page, is 112. What to do after a poisoning, including the UK instruction not to cause vomiting, is on the first-aid poisoning card, not here.
